answer_summary: Single-agent sufficiency wins. The active bundle directly routes guide-reflection maintenance through document-level benchmark/review logic and treats multi-agent or A2A as optional only when material coordination gain is real.
verdict_rationale: The active bundle gives a direct runtime-owned answer path. `CODEX_RUNTIME_GUIDE.md` explicitly defines prompt-stack guide-reflection / benchmark maintenance as primarily a document-level benchmark task, says to stay document-grounded while the live question is doc/runtime parity or benchmark coverage, and exposes replay escalation only when behavior proof or runner state becomes the real issue. The same guide also says `PROMPT_multi_agent_overlay` is added only when decomposition or A2A is itself part of the recommendation, and provides a direct reroute rule to `eval-ops` when the center of gravity becomes benchmark gating or monitored continuation. `PROMPT_multi_agent_overlay.md`, `PROMPT_full.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `orchestration-control/SKILL.md` all explicitly require checking single-agent sufficiency first, forbid forcing multi-agent use on one-coherent-path tasks, and require collapsing back to the simpler route when coordination gain is weak. That is enough to answer this maintenance scenario without operator-only docs, without decorative orchestration, and without widening the patch surface. Stronger replay artifacts are not missing; they are exposed as an explicit fallback route rather than a required first step for this task shape.
limitations: 판정은 활성 번들 문서의 runtime-owned route sufficiency에 대한 검토이며, assembled replay의 실제 실행 상태를 검증한 것은 아니다.
활성 번들에 `eval-ops` 본문이나 evaluation overlay 본문은 없으므로, 그 downstream 실행 세부가 아니라 `CODEX_RUNTIME_GUIDE.md`의 명시적 reroute and escalation 규칙을 근거로 판단했다.
